meta.question: What happens when you type a URL into a browser?
meta.title: From URL to page
meta.author: Web fundamentals notes

answer.headline: The browser finds the server's address (DNS), opens a secure connection (TCP or QUIC, then TLS), asks for the page over HTTP, and then builds and paints the page from the HTML, CSS and JavaScript it receives.
answer.text: On a fast connection this takes a few hundred milliseconds, most of it spent waiting on round trips across the network. Caches at almost every step skip work the browser has done before.
points: DNS turns example.com into an IP address; the answer is usually cached
TLS proves the server is who it claims to be and encrypts everything after
Rendering starts before the download ends: the browser builds the page as bytes arrive

meta.description: Who the browser talks to, in order, from typing the address to the first paint.

data.title: Browser
data.description: Parses the URL, checks its caches, then makes the requests.

data.title: DNS resolver
data.subtitle: Usually your ISP or a public resolver
data.description: Looks up the IP address for the host name, asking other DNS servers if it has no cached answer.

data.title: Web server
data.subtitle: Often a CDN edge
data.description: Terminates TLS and returns the HTML, then the CSS, scripts and images it references.

steps.title: Look up the address
steps.description: If the browser and the operating system have no cached answer, the resolver finds the IP address.

steps.title: Get the IP address
steps.description: The answer comes back with a time to live, so it can be reused.

steps.title: Open a secure connection
steps.description: A TCP (or QUIC) connection, then the TLS handshake starts.

steps.title: Check the certificate
steps.description: The browser checks the certificate matches the name and is signed by a trusted authority, and both sides agree keys.

steps.title: Ask for the page
steps.description: An HTTP request with headers such as cookies and accepted languages.

steps.title: Receive the HTML
steps.description: The browser starts parsing as soon as the first bytes arrive.

steps.title: Fetch what the page needs
steps.description: Stylesheets, scripts and images, often over the same connection, then layout and paint.

blocks.title: Inside the browser, once the HTML arrives

items.title: Parse HTML into the DOM

items.title: Parse CSS into the CSSOM
items.text: Stylesheets block rendering until they have loaded.

items.title: Run JavaScript
items.text: Scripts without `defer` or `async` pause parsing while they run.

items.title: Layout
items.text: Work out the size and position of every element.

items.title: Paint and composite
items.text: Draw pixels in layers and combine them on screen.
